content: The perineal raphe is a distinct anatomical line that extends from the anus, continues along the midline of the scrotum (referred to as the scrotal raphe), and proceeds upward along the posterior midline of the penis (known as the penile raphe). This line is visibly noticeable on physical examination. It forms as a result of a developmental process during fetal growth. During this process, the scrotum, which is the male developmental equivalent of the labia in females, and the penis move toward the midline and fuse together. The fusion of these structures creates a ridge of tissue that is observed as the perineal raphe.
